authority: Product-owner decision authority was explicitly delegated to the Mesh technical lead on 2026-08-03.

candidateBlockers.reason: No clean exact-SHA source candidate with current protected R0 evidence exists. The locally verified implementation remains uncommitted and cannot be bound to the signed draft-candidate lifecycle without owner-authorized commit and protected CI.

D1.summary: The beta must not persist decrypted attachment bytes in Mesh-managed cache storage. Explicit user exports remain user files.

D2.summary: Mesh presents one accountable community owner derived from standard Matrix authority. Ownership transfer is unavailable in beta because immutable creator authority cannot be honestly transferred on all supported room versions.

D3.summary: The beta exposes immediate per-room moderation outcomes but makes no durable or authoritative audit-log claim.

D4.summary: The beta uses standard Matrix invitations and knock flows. The optional managed admission service remains disabled until POST token verification and least-privilege registration issuance are reviewed.

D5.summary: Local account erasure requires a one-use native presence grant. Device revocation and account deactivation additionally require Matrix password reauthentication. Browser-auth account paths and Matrix administrator-role changes fail closed until provider-backed reauthentication is available; routine reversible moderation remains governed by D3 and D9.

D6.summary: NSIS current-user installation is the canonical consumer path and writes a per-user format marker. MSI remains a secondary managed-deployment artifact and writes a per-machine marker. Both UI and silent installers block the opposite format before copying app files, explain uninstall-first recovery, and retain account data by default.

D7.summary: The first beta candidate is v0.2.0, published only as a signed draft prerelease until exact-version acceptance completes. Automatic updates remain off.

D8.summary: Optional Mesh community hosting has no SLA. Publish only measured best-effort targets: 24-hour backup cadence, 24-hour RPO, 12-hour restore target, and 24-hour incident acknowledgement when an operator is available.

D9.summary: The beta ships standard Matrix moderation and transparent rate limits, without global reputation scores or opaque automated anti-raid decisions.

D10.summary: iOS and Android are explicitly unsupported in the first beta and require a separate native product and security contract.

D11.summary: The beta exposes no third-party app or bot platform. A future platform must be deny-by-default, capability-scoped, consented, observable, and revocable.
